chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Details of the 1967 Town Hall concert
summary: Town Hall contacted her; the concert used a Dixieland combination without bass.

blocks.x: Okay. There are two other things
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
to say, to backtrack a little bit. In addition to the Dick Gibson Jazz party, you also told us before, you put on a concert at Town Hall in September of 1967.

No, there was a man that evidently worked at Town Hall and the way I understand it he probably had access to the hall in some kind of way. And he was promoting concerts, different get-togethers down there in which, if you wanted to promote a concert they would print the tickets and you would sell tickets and you'd get fifty-fifty, something like that. So I went down to see him and as I said I hadn't been doing anything and Cliff was here and he thought it over and said it might be a good idea. So we got involved and of course Cliff got out his mailing list and we circulated some little cards, you know, announcing that we would get Town Hall on such and such a date and we did it. We didn't have a big crowd because I had been out of existence for so long I don't think that half the people
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

who got the message thought it was for real. They must have thought it was a joke. But we had about 300 people there which isn't allot of people for Town Hall but it's still allot of people. And I got a very good write-up. John Wilson reviewed it and stated that Maxine Sullivan evokes the swing era and he mentioned the songs that I did. But, more things than just "Loch Lomond." That was a very - I enjoyed that. It was just for a lark, so to speak, but we used Cliff on piano. On several occasions we'd show up at the same place and he would play for me, and I'd sing. We did a thing for the Oversea's Press Club one time, a concert for them one evening. But we never worked together that much except on one occasion. And Cliff was on piano. Max on trumpet. Tony Parente on Clarinet. Marshall Brown on trombone and Sunny Greer on drums. So it was a nice . . .
Was there a bass player there?
In the newspaper clipping that I read about this in, there was no mention of a bass player.
I don't think we used a bass player. We just used the Dixieland combination without bass.
